title: Keep a seat belt anchor's release button pressed while sliding it down its rail past 3 notches, then let it lock
instruction: Lower the seat belt's shoulder anchor to its lowest notch: hold its release button in while sliding it down, let go so it locks, and clear the hands.
context: Anyone who takes a car's front seat can set the shoulder belt anchor: a front-seat occupant lowers it so the belt crosses the shoulder rather than the neck. The press has to last the whole slide: let the button go part way and the lock drops into the nearest notch. The Toyota RAV4 owner's manual gives the act as "To lower: Push in the lock release button and slide the anchor down" and adds "After adjustment, make sure the anchor is locked in position." The United States has 237,655,885 licensed drivers (FHWA Highway Statistics, table DL-22), and Toyota sold 475,193 RAV4s in the United States in 2024 (Toyota Motor North America, 2024 U.S. sales results), each with a height-adjustable shoulder belt anchor at both front seats. Americans make 2.1 trips a day on average (FHWA Mobility Trends briefs, 2022 National Household Travel Survey).
setup: A bench board stands beyond a cut-back table that carries the two arms (bases 61 cm apart): 3/4 in birch plywood (18 mm modelled), 30 x 42 cm, on two 1-1/2 in aluminium round tube posts (about 40 mm modelled), tilted 10 degrees from upright with its top towards the arms, the inward lean of a car's B-pillar. Bolted to it through its rail's two end holes, as it bolts to the pillar: a Toyota RAV4 (2019 to 2025, XA50) front shoulder belt anchor adjuster, Toyota part 73200-12070 (about 75 USD). Its black steel rail (31 mm wide, 25 cm long) carries a black slider (41 mm wide, 85 mm tall) with the anchor stud, collar and nut (dark metal) at its top and a raised block above the white lock release button (21 x 14 mm, 4 mm proud, sprung: 10 N pressed in full) at its lower edge, under the stud. The D-ring guide of a Toyota front belt assembly, 73220-06390-C3, not part of the adjuster (60 mm wide, a 50 x 10 mm webbing slot, rigid; the webbing is left out) hangs from the stud, turned towards the seat side. The stud is 1.16 m above the ground and 30 cm in front of the arm bases at the top notch. The rail has five notches 15 mm apart (60 mm of travel); the anchor starts locked at the top notch. One overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Real-trial checks: after release, a light upward tug of about 5 N does not move the anchor; the video shows the anchor at its lowest notch; a ruler or side photo gives the 10 mm and 3 mm marks.
scoring: 0.33: the anchor at least 10 mm below its top notch (it moves only while the release button is in at least 2 mm, lifting the lock). 0.67: the anchor within 3 mm of the lowest notch. 1.0: the button back out (within 1 mm of its rest), the lock caught in the lowest notch, and both whole grippers (fingers, palm and housing) at least 2 cm from the anchor, held 3 s. The lock catches only within 1.5 mm of a notch, so in the simulation an anchor let go between notches stays free and scores at most 0.67. Void (0): the anchor forced more than 3 mm off a notch while locked (checked from 0.5 s after the lock catches). Real trial: a ruler or side photo for the 10 mm and 3 mm marks; a light upward tug (about 5 N) on the anchor must not move it; the video must show it at the lowest notch.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz, GPU. Board and rail fixed. Anchor: 0.22 kg, weight left out (gravity off), prismatic joint along the rail, 60 mm travel, joint friction 0.5 N. Button: prismatic joint, 4 mm travel, 2500 N/m (10 N). Lock pawl is code: button in 2 mm frees the anchor; button out (within 1 mm) catches a notch only within 1.5 mm (50 kN/m, held to 2000 N). Estimates bounded in the README; 1.0 at both range ends. Sizes from the maker's photo. Webbing left out.
scores: demo: 1.0 (344 steps, 17.2 s); Dream-1: 0.0 (the model did not press the button)
